case_name: N. Jayaram Reddy and Another v Revenue Divisional Officer and Land Acquisition Officer, Kurnool
respondent:
Revenue Divisional Officer and Land Acquisition Officer, Kurnool
Supreme Court of India

23 March 1979
Civil Appeal No. 2314 of 1969
The Judgment was delivered by : P. N. Shingal, J.
1. This appeal is by a certificate of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh on the valuation of the subject matter and is directed against its judgment dated February 4, 1969.
2. The State Government acquired 2 acres and 79 cents of the land of the appellants in Kurnool town, for locating a bus depot of the Andhra Pradesh State Transport Corporation. It was arable land within the municipal limits of the town, with two trees and an old compound wall. Its possession was taken by the State Government on May 25, 1962. The market value of the land was fixed at Rs. 27,042.53 at the rate of Rs. 2/- per square yard. facts: The State Government acquired 2 acres and 79 cents of land from the appellants in Kurnool town for locating a bus depot.
The market value of the land was fixed at Rs. 27,042.53 at the rate of Rs. 2/- per square yard.

N. Jayarama Reddy, Y. Prabhakar Reddy and C. Manikya Reddy were the three owners of the land who accepted the compensation under protest and applied for a reference under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.

After recording evidence and inspecting the site, the Subordinate Judge held that the claimants were entitled to payment at the rate of Rs. 12/- per square yard for the value of land, a solatium of 15 per cent and interest at 4 per cent.
issues: Whether the government appeal abated against the deceased respondent Y. Prabhakar Reddy
Whether the High Court's decree dated February 4, 1969 was a nullity merely because it was passed against a dead person
petitioner_arguments: The appeal before the High Court was directed against the joint decree and the appellate court could not take a decision on the basis of the separate shares of the claimants
The whole of the government appeal should have been dismissed because of its abatement against the deceased respondent
respondent_arguments: The decree against a dead person is not necessarily a nullity for all purposes

It will be sufficient to say that such a decree has been held to be a nullity because it cannot be executed against his legal representative for the simple reason that he did not have a full opportunity of being heard in respect of it
court_reasoning: The law has provided and accepted modes for reopening and hearing the appeal in such cases
A decree against a dead person is treated as a nullity because it cannot be allowed to operate against his legal representative when he was never brought on the record to defend the case
holding: The High Court's decree dated February 4, 1969 was not a nullity merely because it was passed against a dead person
The government appeal did not abate against the deceased respondent Y. Prabhakar Reddy
